## Demonstrating that the Area Under the Student's *t*-Distribution Equals 1

The Student's *t*-distribution with \(\nu\) degrees of freedom has the probability density function (PDF):

\[
f(t) = \frac{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{\nu+1}{2}\right)}{\sqrt{\nu\pi}\,\Gamma\!\left(\frac{\nu}{2}\right)} \left(1+\frac{t^2}{\nu}\right)^{-\frac{\nu+1}{2}}.
\]

This R code:
1. Plots the *t*-distribution curve for a chosen degree of freedom.  
2. Numerically integrates the PDF over \((-∞, ∞)\) to confirm that the total area under the curve is equal to 1.  
3. Shades the region under the curve to visually represent this area.

---

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Set degrees of freedom
nu <- 5

# Create a sequence of t-values
t_vals <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 400)

# Compute PDF values using built-in dt() function
pdf_vals <- dt(t_vals, df = nu)

# Create a data frame for plotting
df <- data.frame(t = t_vals, density = pdf_vals)

# Numerically integrate to confirm total area = 1
area <- integrate(function(x) dt(x, df = nu), -Inf, Inf)$value

# Display the computed area
cat("Numerically computed area under the t-distribution (df =", nu, "):", area, "\n")

# Plot the t-distribution and shade under the curve
ggplot(df, aes(x = t, y = density)) +
  geom_area(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Student's t-Distribution (df = ", nu, ")"),
    subtitle = "Shaded area under the curve ≈ 1",
    x = "t value",
    y = "Density"
  )
```
